stories.head: Paytm gets RBI's in-principle nod to run wallets again; shares close at ₹1,939.70, about 10% below the ₹2,150 IPO price
stories.dek: Two and a half years after the Payments Bank crackdown took its wallet away, Paytm is a step closer to getting it back, and its stock is nearly back where it listed.
stat: share price; the IPO price was ₹2,150

sections.title: What RBI approved
paras: The Reserve Bank of India has given Paytm Payments Services Ltd (PPSL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Paytm's parent One 97 Communications, an in-principle approval to issue and run prepaid payment instruments. That category covers digital wallets, the product that made Paytm a household name.

It is not the final green light yet. PPSL has to submit a system and cybersecurity audit within six months, or the approval lapses, and it still needs final authorisation from the RBI before it can issue a single wallet. Paytm applied in July 2026.

sections.title: Why it's a big deal
paras: Paytm's wallet effectively went dark after the RBI's January 2024 action against Paytm Payments Bank, which barred it from taking fresh deposits, including wallet top-ups. According to Entrackr, the RBI later cancelled the Payments Bank's licence on 24 April 2026. A wallet licence under a different company is the clearest sign yet of a regulatory comeback.

sections.title: The stock story
paras: Paytm shares closed at ₹1,939.70 on Friday, up about 7.7% over two sessions and close to a 52-week high of ₹1,960. That is about 9.8% below the ₹2,150 price at which it listed in 2021, and more than double its 52-week low of ₹930.60 in March.

The business has also turned around: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28.5% to ₹2,648 crore and net profit came in at ₹225 crore, its sixth profitable quarter in a row. Brokerage Bernstein raised its target price to ₹2,200 from ₹1,500.

sections.title: What's next
paras: Watch for the audit and the RBI's final authorisation. For users, it could mean the familiar Paytm wallet returning for small, quick payments alongside UPI.

stories.head: Maybelline rewrites its famous 'Maybe she's born with it' tagline after 35 years: it's now 'Maybe. We're born with it.'
stories.dek: One of advertising's best-known lines just lost a pronoun, and marketers are already debating what the swap says.
stat: since the original line launched in 1991

sections.title: What changed
paras: Maybelline New York has quietly updated the slogan it has used on and off since 1991. The old line was "Maybe she's born with it. Maybe it's Maybelline." The new one reads "Maybe. We're born with it. Maybe. It's Maybelline."

The edit is tiny on paper: 'she's' becomes 'we're', and the line is broken up with full stops. But in branding terms it shifts the voice from talking about a woman to speaking as a group that includes the reader.

sections.title: Why the line matters
paras: Few taglines are as famous. CBS Outdoor once ranked it the most recognisable tagline of the past 150 years. Maybelline dropped it in 2015 for "Make It Happen", then brought it back in 2024, and has now reworked it again.
afaqs, which reported the change, reads it as a move towards a more inclusive, gender-neutral message. That is the publication's interpretation; Maybelline has not been quoted explaining the reason.

sections.title: A 111-year-old brand
paras: The brand began in 1915 as Lash-Brow-Ine. Founder Thomas Lyle Williams later renamed it by joining his sister Mabel's name with Vaseline. L'Oréal bought it in 1996 and added 'New York' to the name.

sections.title: The takeaway for marketers
paras: Legacy brands rarely touch a line people can sing back to them. Maybelline kept the rhythm and the 'Maybe' hook, and changed just one word, a low-risk way to modernise without losing the memory.

stories.head: Royal Enfield sells a record 3.77 lakh bikes in a quarter; Eicher's Q2 profit rises 14.9% to ₹1,573 crore
stories.dek: India's favourite big-bike brand had its best quarter ever, though profit still came in a little below what analysts expected.
stat: motorcycles sold in Q2, its best ever

sections.title: The numbers
paras: Eicher Motors, which owns Royal Enfield, reported a 14.9% rise in July–September profit to ₹1,573 crore on Friday, 13 November. Revenue grew 20.3% to ₹7,422 crore and EBITDA hit a record ₹1,760 crore.
Royal Enfield sold 3,76,722 motorcycles in the quarter, up 15.2% and the most it has ever sold in three months. First-half profit was ₹3,036 crore, up 17.9%.

sections.title: The catch
paras: Margins slipped. The EBITDA margin fell to 23.7% from 24.5% a year ago, and profit missed the LSEG analyst estimate of ₹1,626 crore. Royal Enfield has raised prices four times in 2026, including a 0.7% increase in October.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Royal Enfield holds around 84% of India's mid-size motorcycle segment, the 250–750cc bikes that young buyers increasingly upgrade to. A record quarter shows that demand for its Classics, Bullets and Hunters is still growing even after several price increases.
The brand is also preparing for an electric future: its Flying Flea C6 EV has added 10 new dealers.

sections.title: What to watch
paras: The festive season fell partly in October, so the next quarter's numbers will show whether the record run continues and whether the price increases start to hurt demand.

stories.head: India bowled out for 89 as New Zealand win the 4th ODI by 244 runs; Matt Henry takes six wickets
stories.dek: India needed one win to seal the series, and crashed inside 27 overs instead. Sunday's final game at the same ground now decides it.

sections.title: What happened
paras: At Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on Friday, 13 November, New Zealand piled up 333 all out in 50 overs. Opener Will Young led the way with 125 off 108 balls, hitting 14 fours and 4 sixes.

Chasing 334, India collapsed to 89 all out in 26.4 overs. Fast bowler Matt Henry took six wickets and was named Player of the Match. He removed Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and captain Shreyas Iyer early, and the chase never recovered.

sections.title: The scorecard story
paras: Ishan Kishan was India's top scorer with just 27 off 53 balls. Matthew Fisher chipped in with three wickets for New Zealand.

sections.title: Series state
paras: India still lead the five-match series 2-1. They had won the first two games, and the third in Hamilton was washed out, so this was New Zealand's first win of the series.

sections.title: What's next
paras: The decider is on Sunday, 15 November, again at Bay Oval, starting 7:30 am IST. India need to win to take the series; a New Zealand win would make it 2-2.

stories.head: Domino's UK trolls Manchester United again, with a pizza-box reel after the club sacks Michael Carrick
stories.dek: The pizza chain has made mocking United a running joke, and its latest post landed within hours of the club's managerial change.

sections.title: The post
paras: After Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick, Domino's UK posted an Instagram reel showing raw pizza ingredients being shaken around inside a pizza box. The caption joked about "whoever United appoint next trying to cook up something special", followed by a simple "Good luck."
The joke works because it says two things at once: United's next boss is starting with a messy box of ingredients, and Domino's is the expert at turning those into something people want.

sections.title: Why United are an easy target
paras: United are in the Premier League relegation zone, with one league win in their first 10 matches. Reports say the club is close to hiring Mauricio Pochettino, but nothing has been announced.

sections.title: A long-running bit
paras: This is not a one-off. Domino's UK put out a 'We're hiring (not you, Erik)' van in 2024 aimed at then-manager Erik ten Hag, posted after United's loss to Brighton in September 2026, and predicted in August 2026 that United would be relegated.

sections.title: The marketing lesson
paras: Topical banter like this costs little and travels fast because fans of rival clubs share it. The risk is annoying United supporters, but Domino's has clearly decided the attention is worth it. Indian brands like Amul and Zomato use the same playbook around cricket and pop culture.

stories.head: India's exports jump nearly 30% to $89.99 billion in October; overall trade deficit narrows to $20.09 billion
stories.dek: Goods exports rose 45% from a year ago, while a strong services surplus kept the combined gap in check.

sections.title: The data
paras: Commerce Ministry figures released on 13 November show India's total exports of goods and services were $89.99 billion in October 2026, up from $69.27 billion a year earlier. Total imports rose to $110.07 billion from $94.42 billion, so the overall trade deficit narrowed to $20.09 billion from $25.15 billion.
Merchandise exports alone rose 45.06% to $49.47 billion. Goods imports were $89.35 billion, leaving a goods-only gap of about $39.88 billion.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: The headline narrowing comes from adding goods and services together. Services exports, estimated at $40.51 billion against imports of $20.72 billion, produced a surplus of about $20 billion that offset much of the goods deficit. High oil prices are still keeping the import bill elevated.

stories.head: India's forex reserves rise $2.49 billion to $719.55 billion as gold holdings climb to $104.8 billion
stories.dek: Most of the weekly gain came from the higher value of gold, not fresh dollar buying.

sections.title: The numbers
paras: RBI data released on 13 November show India's foreign exchange reserves rose $2.49 billion to $719.55 billion in the week ended 6 November. Gold reserves rose about $2.21 billion to $104.8 billion, while foreign currency assets added $232 million to $591.35 billion.
Reserves are $32.51 billion higher than a year ago.

sections.title: The bigger picture
paras: Reserves are still about $66 billion below the all-time high of $785.7 billion reached in the week ended 4 September 2026. They fell for several weeks as the RBI sold dollars to steady the rupee, which is trading near record lows around 94 to the dollar.

stories.head: Dubai airport halts SpiceJet check-ins over about ₹35.8 crore in unpaid dues; Dubai–India flights cancelled
stories.dek: If you hold a SpiceJet ticket from Dubai, check your booking: the airline has been told to rebook passengers and provide hotels.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Dubai Airports stopped checking in SpiceJet passengers from 12 November over unpaid charges of AED 14 million, about ₹35.8 crore. It says SpiceJet has not paid since 13 October and missed a deadline after a warning on 9 November.
Four flights to Amritsar, Jaipur, Mumbai and Delhi were cancelled on 12 November, and reports say no SpiceJet flight left Dubai for India on Friday.

sections.title: What it means for passengers
paras: Dubai's aviation regulator summoned SpiceJet's station manager and ordered the airline to inform passengers, rebook them, and provide hotels and transport. SpiceJet is flying about 65 flights a day overall and cancelling 15–20 daily, according to Business Today, as it battles money troubles.

stories.credit: NTA exam centre / via India Today
stories.head: After the NEET-UG leak, NTA will build a permanent pool of independent exam observers, including retired armed forces personnel
stories.dek: Observers will report straight to the testing agency instead of local exam staff, for exams like NEET-UG, JEE Main and CUET.

sections.title: The plan
paras: The National Testing Agency has invited expressions of interest for a standing pool of exam observers and for exam centres. Three groups can apply: retired central and state government officers; retired armed forces and paramilitary personnel; and retired or serving government teachers and professors.
Observers will report directly to NTA rather than to city coordinators or centre superintendents. At centres abroad, Indian nationals living in the same city will be empanelled.

sections.title: Why now
paras: The move follows this year's NEET-UG paper leak and aims to make supervision independent of local centre staff. NTA is also hiring for 13 senior posts on deputation, including seven directors; applications close on 1 December.

stories.head: Delhi's air turns 'severe' with AQI at 403 on Friday morning; GRAP Stage III curbs stay in force
stories.dek: The capital's air hovered around the severe mark through the day as winter pollution set in.

sections.title: The reading
paras: Delhi's Air Quality Index crossed into the 'severe' category at 403 on the morning of 13 November, according to Central Pollution Control Board data reported by The Wire. It eased slightly to 394 by 2:05 pm, still in the 'very poor' band, just below severe.

sections.title: What's in place
paras: Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) has been in force across the National Capital Region since 6 November. It brings curbs such as limits on construction and demolition work and restrictions on some older vehicles. Doctors advise people with breathing problems, children and older adults to limit time outdoors and use masks when they must go out.

stories.head: US halts every departing flight nationwide for hours; over 4,000 cancellations and 10,000+ delays
stories.dek: The FAA blamed a 'telecommunication outage' in air traffic control systems. Officials said there was no sign of foul play.

sections.title: What happened
paras: The US Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop on all departing flights on Friday, 13 November, at 3:54 pm ET, citing "extraordinary circumstances" and safety. It was lifted at 8:15 pm ET. FlightAware showed more than 4,000 cancellations and over 10,000 delays.

The FAA and the White House called the cause a "telecommunication outage". Transport Secretary Sean Duffy blamed "an incredibly old air traffic control system" whose routers were overloaded with data.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: It was the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023. Homeland Security said there was no indication the outage was malicious. Knock-on delays were expected through the weekend, including for international travellers connecting through US airports.

stories.head: Iran says it destroyed a US radar in Bahrain; US Central Command says both Iranian drones were shot down with no damage
stories.dek: The two sides gave opposite accounts, as Gulf states urge Washington to hold off on wider strikes.

sections.title: Two versions
paras: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said on 13 November that it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, calling it retaliation for a US strike a day earlier on a telecoms tower in southern Iran's Hormozgan province. US Central Command said two Iranian one-way attack drones were launched toward Bahrain and both were shot down, with "no injuries or damage". Bahrain hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet.

sections.title: The wider picture
paras: President Trump said Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, the UAE and Bahrain had asked him to postpone broader attacks on Iran, and that he was holding off for now. The US naval blockade of Iranian ports remains in place. Qatar and Pakistan are still trying to mediate.

stories.head: Europe will join the next round of US-brokered Russia–Ukraine talks; US works toward the 'largest prisoner exchange of the war'
stories.dek: After meeting Putin, US envoys Witkoff and Kushner flew to Ireland to brief Zelensky.

sections.title: What's new
paras: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky near Dublin on 12 November, straight after their talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Kushner said both sides agreed to widen the next round to include European partners, and Witkoff said Putin had agreed to let European representatives join.
Kushner also said the US is working toward the "largest prisoner exchange of the war". No numbers were given; Zelensky called it "a real result".

sections.title: Still unresolved
paras: No date or venue has been set for the next round. Territory remains the main sticking point: Russia holds about a fifth of Ukraine and Kyiv refuses to give up the rest of the Donbas. Attacks by both sides continued while the talks went on.

stories.head: Gaza's winter crisis: 150,000 tents are stuck at the borders as dozens of nations urge Israel to ease aid limits
stories.dek: Rain is flooding tents in Khan Younis, and the UN says about 3.5 lakh displaced people face freezing conditions.

sections.title: The situation
paras: UN aid chief Tom Fletcher says 150,000 tents are waiting at Gaza's borders while about 350,000 displaced people face flooding and cold. Most of Gaza's roughly 2 million people live in tents or makeshift shelters. A nine-month-old boy died of hypothermia this week after his family's tent in Khan Younis flooded, aid groups reported.

sections.title: The diplomatic push
paras: A joint statement read at the UN on 12 November by the UK's envoy, backed by about 49 countries (some outlets count 53 countries and organisations), asked Israel to ease limits on shelter, fuel, water, sanitation and medical items. The US did not sign. Israel's UN ambassador rejected the initiative and blamed Hamas, and Prime Minister Netanyahu said Israel has allowed in 91,000 tents.

facts: Living in shelters: most of ~2 mn

stories.head: Tata Motors PV posts record ₹20,400 crore India revenue as EV sales jump 90%, but JLR charges push it into a loss
stories.dek: The Indian car business, led by the Sierra and EVs, is booming. Jaguar Land Rover is the drag.

sections.title: India is flying
paras: Tata Motors' passenger vehicle business reported record India revenue of ₹20,400 crore for July–September, up 51%. It is now India's No. 2 carmaker with a 14.3% share. EV volumes rose about 90% to around 15,700 a month, giving Tata 42.8% of India's electric car market.
The new Tata Sierra has sold 70,000 units since January, and October was a record month with 75,400 vehicles.

sections.title: The JLR problem
paras: Consolidated revenue rose 34% to about ₹96,900 crore, but exceptional charges of about ₹6,700 crore pushed the company into a net loss. Jaguar Land Rover's revenue rose 20.3% to £5.89 billion; the Defender sold 30,000 units while Jaguar sold just 800 as it transitions to an all-electric brand. The stock fell about 3.3% on Friday.

stories.head: Sachin Tendulkar invests in recycling startup Recykal, which made ₹1,498 crore in revenue last year
stories.dek: The cricket legend's newest bet is a waste-management platform used by brands like HUL, Samsung and BMW.

sections.title: The deal
paras: Sachin Tendulkar has invested an undisclosed amount in Hyderabad-based Recykal as a strategic investor, through an extension of its recently closed $23 million bridge round. Recykal has raised more than $60 million in total, from backers including Morgan Stanley, 360 ONE, Circulate Capital and the Murugappa group.

sections.title: The business
paras: Recykal connects waste generators with more than 5,000 aggregators and recyclers and works with about 650 brands. Its FY26 gross revenue rose 53.2% to ₹1,498 crore from ₹978 crore, while its loss widened 7% to ₹60 crore.
It is Tendulkar's second startup bet in about two weeks after gaming company Hitwicket; his portfolio also includes Spinny and Kissht.

stories.head: SoftBank sells another 1.65% of Meesho for ₹1,885 crore in a block deal; Fidelity, GIC and Norges Bank buy in
stories.dek: Big global funds are lining up for India's newly listed consumer internet stocks.

sections.title: The deal
paras: SoftBank sold 7.64 crore Meesho shares at ₹246.75 each on 13 November, about 4% below the previous close of ₹257.07. Buyers included Fidelity, Societe Generale, Norges Bank, Singapore's GIC and HDFC Mutual Fund. SoftBank's stake falls from 6.84% to about 5.19%. It had already sold 1.73% for ₹1,650 crore in September.

sections.title: Meesho's numbers
paras: Meesho is worth about ₹1.19 lakh crore on the stock market. In July–September its revenue rose 38% to ₹4,132 crore and its loss narrowed 68% to ₹132 crore. It is also being added to the MSCI India Standard Index, which can bring in money from index-tracking funds.

stories.head: Razorpay's founders lose a Karnataka High Court bid to quash an SFIO case, ahead of a ₹5,000–6,000 crore IPO
stories.dek: The case is about loan-app payments from years ago; Razorpay itself is not named as an accused.

sections.title: The ruling
paras: The Karnataka High Court has rejected a plea by Razorpay co-founders Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar to quash a Serious Fraud Investigation Office case. It relates to alleged know-your-customer lapses in onboarding Mad Elephant Network Technology, a firm accused of running illegal digital lending and making wrongful gains of ₹56.63 crore. The government's lawyer said about ₹320 crore of its transactions went through Razorpay.
Razorpay says it has "no association with these entities", calls it a five-year-old loan-app case, and will pursue legal remedies.

sections.title: The IPO
paras: SEBI cleared Razorpay's IPO on 3 November. The ₹5,000–6,000 crore issue values it at about $5 billion and is expected to list between January and March 2027.

stories.head: ACKO now puts about 80% of its media spend into creators and connected TV, says its CMO
stories.dek: The insurance brand has moved away from traditional TV over 18 months, and is preparing for AI search.
stat: of ACKO's media spend on creators + CTV

sections.title: The shift
paras: ACKO's chief marketing officer Nitin Khanna told afaqs the insurer moved about 80% of its media budget to creators and connected TV over the past 18 months. Its connected-TV push targets 25–30 million households in India's top 10–15 cities, and its new campaign has three films with creators including Jordindian and Vishaka Biswas.

sections.title: What's working
paras: Testing Google's AI Max lifted car-insurance leads by 8% and bike-insurance leads by 21%, the company says. ACKO is also shifting from classic SEO toward being found in AI-generated answers, but says it is cautious about advertising inside ChatGPT. Cricketer MS Dhoni is both a brand ambassador and an investor.

stories.head: Google puts ₹10 crore into creator-economy startup Rigi at a ₹670 crore valuation
stories.dek: A small but strategic cheque as India's microdrama and creator-video race heats up.

sections.title: The deal
paras: Google International has been allotted 1,543 preference shares in Rigi at ₹61,796 each, about ₹10 crore in total, for a 1.43% stake, according to filings reported by Entrackr. That values the Bengaluru startup at about ₹670 crore.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Rigi helps creators earn from their audiences and has moved into microdramas, the short vertical-video series that apps like QuickTV are scaling quickly. Its last big round was about ₹100 crore in January 2023, led by Elevation. In FY25 it reported revenue of ₹19.92 crore and a net loss of ₹20.5 crore.

stories.head: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster model it says finishes tasks 2.5x quicker than Gemini 3.8 Flash
stories.dek: It is rolling out across the Gemini app, Search and developer tools at once, priced at $1.50 per million input tokens.
stat: faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash, says Google

sections.title: What it is
paras: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on 12 November as the fast, lower-cost tier of its Gemini 4 family, replacing Gemini 3.8 Flash. It is aimed at coding, documents and AI agents that carry out multi-step tasks. Google says it scores 57% on the Terminal-Bench 4.1 coding test, against 18.2% for 3.8 Flash.
It is available through the Gemini app, Google Search, AI Studio, the Gemini API and Android Studio, with a context window of about 1 million tokens.

sections.title: Pricing
paras: Developers pay $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, with batch use at half price. That is more expensive than older Flash models, a sign Google is betting buyers will pay for speed and smarter agents.

stories.head: Nvidia fallout reaches the US Senate: Commerce Secretary Lutnick to testify on 10 December over AI chip sales to China
stories.dek: Lawmakers want to know how a Singapore firm bought over $4.8 billion of Nvidia chips that may have reached China.
stat: of Nvidia chips bought by Megaspeed

sections.title: What's new
paras: Senate Banking Committee chair Tim Scott has asked Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify on 10 December, and his spokesperson said he agreed to appear voluntarily. Scott has also asked former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to testify on 3 December.

The focus is Megaspeed International, a Singapore company that bought more than $4.8 billion of advanced Nvidia AI chips over two years. US officials suspect some were diverted to China, and lawmakers are asking why Commerce delayed adding it to a trade blacklist.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Huang resigned on 12 November; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and Harvey C. Jones is Nvidia's first board chair. Senators from both parties are now pressing on export controls, which could shape future US rules on selling AI chips abroad. Nvidia shares fell another 2% on Friday and closed below $4 trillion in market value.

stories.head: Andhra Pradesh signs ₹1.41 lakh crore of deals in a day, led by a 1,400 MW data-centre campus; Agnikul plans orbital data centres in Tirupati
stories.dek: Visakhapatnam and Tirupati are pitching themselves as hubs for AI data centres and space tech.
stat: deals signed on day 2 of the summit

sections.title: The deals
paras: On 13 November, day two of the CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh signed 12 agreements worth ₹1,41,585 crore, expected to create about 10,919 jobs. The biggest was AirTrunk India with JCK Infra, for 1,400 MW of data-centre campuses worth ₹1,03,018 crore. Dixon Technologies committed ₹700 crore.

sections.title: Data centres in space
paras: IIT Madras-incubated rocket startup Agnikul Cosmos signed an MoU for a ₹510 crore facility in Tirupati district, with 350 jobs, to build platforms for orbital data centres. Agnikul plans to turn the upper stage of its Agnibaan rocket into a host for computing hardware in orbit. The idea is still experimental, and some in the industry question the economics.

stories.head: Microsoft 365 outage knocks out Outlook, Teams and Copilot in at least 74 countries for a second workday
stories.dek: Indian firms including IndiGo and Akasa Air reported disruption; Microsoft says there's no sign of a cyberattack.

sections.title: What broke
paras: The outage began on Thursday, 12 November, and hit Exchange Online email, Teams, SharePoint, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Defender. Microsoft said servers had "unexpectedly become unavailable" and a core process was being overwhelmed. It paused all deployments, rerouted traffic and restarted servers. By Friday afternoon US time, email queues were close to normal, with some issues remaining.

sections.title: Impact in India
paras: Inc42 reports that IndiGo, Akasa Air, HR software firm Keka and Equitas Small Finance Bank were among Indian businesses affected, and Downdetector logged about 2,157 complaints from India late on Thursday night. Microsoft said it found no sign of malicious activity and has not yet disclosed the root cause.

stories.head: Sensex falls 319 points to 81,592 and Nifty ends at 25,144, snapping a three-day winning streak
stories.dek: Oil worries and the jump in retail inflation weighed on rate-sensitive stocks; FMCG was the only sector in the green.

sections.title: The close
paras: The Sensex fell 318.56 points, or 0.39%, to 81,592.45 on Friday, 13 November. The Nifty 50 dropped 155.05 points, or 0.61%, to 25,144.30. Every sector index fell except FMCG; auto, metal and realty lost about 1% each.
Shriram Finance (-3.37%) and Tata Motors PV (-3.31%) were the biggest Nifty losers, while Eicher Motors (+1.34%) and HUL (+0.96%) led the gainers.

sections.title: Why
paras: Brent crude stayed near $96 after attacks on Saudi energy sites, and October's 6.09% retail inflation raised fears of an RBI rate hike. Still, both indices ended the week higher for a third week in a row: the Sensex rose 0.7% and the Nifty 0.5%. Foreign investors have kept buying, with November inflows the highest since December 2020.

stories.head: Rupee weakens 21 paise to 94.24 against the dollar as US yields and crude rise
stories.dek: Hot US inflation data and bets on a December Fed hike lifted the dollar; strong foreign buying limited the fall.
stat: rupee per US dollar, Friday close

sections.title: The move
paras: The rupee closed at 94.24 per dollar on Friday, 13 November, down 21 paise from 94.03, according to HDFC Sky's market wrap. The dollar index rose to about 103.2, near a 19-month high, after US inflation data came in hot. Traders are pricing in a high chance of a US Federal Reserve rate hike in December.

sections.title: What's holding it
paras: Steady buying of Indian shares by foreign investors kept the rupee from sliding further. Dealers expect it to trade between roughly 93.85 and 94.60 in the near term, with oil prices and Gulf tensions the main risks.

stories.head: Wall Street ends mixed: Nasdaq falls 0.91% as Nvidia slides again and US wholesale inflation hits 6.5%
stories.dek: Tech stocks fell while consumer staples and energy held the Dow up, but all three indices still gained over the week.

sections.title: The close
paras: On Friday, 13 November, the Dow edged up 0.1% to 52,347.55, the S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,561.67 and the Nasdaq dropped 0.91% to 25,136.27. Tech was the worst sector, down 1.7%. Nvidia fell another 2% and closed below $4 trillion in market value for the first time since July 2025.

sections.title: The inflation problem
paras: US producer prices rose 0.3% in October and 6.5% from a year earlier, the highest since November 2022. Combined with the earlier consumer price data, that is pushing up bets on a Fed rate hike. Over the week, the S&P 500 still rose 2.5%, the Dow 2.1% and the Nasdaq 2.3%.

stories.head: India finish the Dakar Youth Olympics with 10 medals, their second-best haul ever, including first-ever boxing golds
stories.dek: A small team of 17 athletes brought home medals in seven sports, with several Indian firsts.

sections.title: The haul
paras: India ended the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, on 13 November with 10 medals: 2 gold, 3 silver and 5 bronze. Only the 2018 Games, with 13 medals, were better. Boxers Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei (boys' 50kg) and Gunjan (girls' 48kg) won India's first-ever Youth Olympic boxing golds.

Silvers came in judo and badminton, among others. Swimmer Dhinidhi Desinghu won two bronzes, becoming the first Indian with two medals at a single edition, and Shourya Ambure won India's first Youth Olympic athletics medal in the 100m hurdles.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: India sent just 17 athletes in 11 sports, and nine of them won medals. Many are products of the Khelo India programme. These were the first Olympic-movement Games ever held in Africa.

stories.head: Lakshya Sen beats home player Yushi Tanaka 21-16, 21-15 to reach the Kumamoto Masters semi-finals; Srikanth is out
stories.dek: India's last player in the draw now faces Indonesia's Alwi Farhan, who has beaten him twice before.

sections.title: The quarter-final
paras: Eighth seed Lakshya Sen beat Japan's Yushi Tanaka 21-16, 21-15 in about 40 minutes on Friday, 13 November, at the Kumamoto Masters, a Super 500 event in Japan. Kidambi Srikanth, who had upset fifth seed Kodai Naraoka a round earlier, lost his quarter-final to Japan's Koki Watanabe in straight games after a tight first game.

sections.title: Up next
paras: Lakshya plays Indonesia's sixth seed Alwi Farhan in the semi-final on Saturday, 14 November, around 7:20 am IST. Farhan has won both of their previous meetings. The winner meets Koki Watanabe or second seed Kunlavut Vitidsarn in the final.

stories.head: Ramayana: Part 1 reaches about ₹1,110 crore worldwide in 9 days, with ₹47.85 crore net on its second Friday
stories.dek: Nitesh Tiwari's epic held strongly on day 9, and its second weekend should push it further.

sections.title: The numbers
paras: According to Sacnilk, Ramayana: Part 1 earned ₹47.85 crore net in India on its ninth day, Friday 13 November, down just 10.6% from day 8. Hindi brought in ₹36.25 crore of that, with the rest from the Malayalam, Kannada, Tamil and Telugu versions.
Its India net total stands at ₹612.45 crore (₹732.20 crore gross), and overseas earnings are estimated at ₹378.50 crore, taking the worldwide total to about ₹1,110.70 crore.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: The film, starring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash, opened on 5 November and crossed ₹1,000 crore worldwide in eight days. A second Friday this strong suggests it has a long run ahead. Sacnilk notes overseas numbers are rough estimates.

stories.head: Dhanush and Mammootty's Tamil action thriller OM drops its trailer; in cinemas worldwide on 20 November
stories.dek: The next big Tamil release arrives in a week, with Sai Pallavi also in the cast.

sections.title: The film
paras: OM – Chapter 1: Udhiram – The Blood Wood is a Tamil action thriller directed by Rajkumar Periasamy, starring Dhanush and Mammootty, with Sai Pallavi. It is produced by Wunderbar Films and RTake Studios. The trailer came out on 13 November, and the film releases worldwide on 20 November.

sections.title: The box-office backdrop
paras: It arrives as Ramayana: Part 1 dominates cinemas and Suriya's Scene has crossed ₹200 crore worldwide. Friday's smaller Telugu openers, such as Donga Naa Koduku, made around ₹1 crore net on day one, according to early Sacnilk estimates.

stories.head: A Bengaluru teen turned a government school's storage room into a library of over 2,000 books
stories.dek: Asavari Agrawal, 17, has spent nearly five years of weekends making it happen, and partly paid for it by selling her piano.
stat: books in the new school library

sections.title: The library
paras: Asavari Agrawal started her initiative 'Shape the Future' at 13. Over nearly five years of weekend visits to a government school in Mullur Colony, Bengaluru, she and five student volunteers collected more than 2,000 books and turned a storage room into a library the children can call their own.

sections.title: How far it reaches
paras: The effort now reaches about 250 children, with around 50 student volunteers in the wider network and 10–15 turning up for Saturday sessions. It is entirely self-funded: Asavari sold her piano and table-tennis table to help pay for it. On Children's Day, it's a reminder that kids can change things for other kids.

stories.head: A new scorpion species has been found in Odisha's Similipal Tiger Reserve, the first of its kind recorded in the state
stories.dek: Named Liocheles similipalensis, it's a reminder of how much of India's wildlife is still undiscovered.
stat: known species in the genus now

sections.title: The find
paras: Researchers have described a new scorpion, Liocheles similipalensis, named after Similipal Tiger Reserve in Mayurbhanj district. It is 44–53 mm long, with a dark black body and a bluish sheen, and lives in moist forest among rocks at about 1,000 m altitude. It is the first Liocheles species confirmed in Odisha, and the genus now has seven known species.

sections.title: Teamwork
paras: Forest staff first collected the specimens and sent them to specialists at the Thackeray Wildlife Foundation, who described it with Similipal's field director. So far the species is known only from the reserve.

stories.head: All five Indian students win medals, including 2 golds, at the Junior Astronomy Olympiad in Thailand
stories.dek: 104 students from 25 countries competed; every member of India's team came home with a medal.

sections.title: The results
paras: At the 5th International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics for Juniors in Ubon Ratchathani, Thailand (1–8 November), Siddharth Laxmisha from Puducherry and Swara Srujal Patel from Gujarat won gold. Aarna Chaplot from Kota and Krish Bhaskar from Bagar in Rajasthan won silver, and Akshara Gulab Ambone from Maharashtra won bronze.

sections.title: Made in Kolkata
paras: The National Council of Science Museums selected and trained the team, with its training camp held at Kolkata's Birla Industrial & Technological Museum.

stories.head: An Indian-made 'surgical GPS' has helped in over 20,000 operations across 200+ hospitals
stories.dek: Bengaluru's HRS Navigation built a cheaper alternative to imported systems, so precise surgery can reach smaller cities.

sections.title: How it works
paras: HRS Navigation, founded in Bengaluru in 2015 by Arpit and Shweta Paliwal, makes easyNav. It builds a 3D map of the patient from CT scans and uses infrared cameras to track a surgeon's instruments in real time, helping locate tumours and see how close they are to nerves and blood vessels.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Such systems are mostly imported and costly, often with extra charges for every procedure. easyNav fits into existing operating theatres and avoids those per-surgery costs. The company says it is now in more than 200 hospitals.

stories.head: A rare Central Asian white stork, from a population of under 2,000, has been spotted at Okhla Bird Sanctuary
stories.dek: Birdwatchers are flocking to the Yamuna wetland near Noida to see a visitor last recorded in Delhi-NCR in 2019.

sections.title: The sighting
paras: Birder Tejaswi first spotted the stork on 1 November at the Noida entrance of Okhla Bird Sanctuary, and it stayed for at least three days. It is believed to be the rare Central Asian subspecies, which breeds mainly in Uzbekistan and southern Kazakhstan and is estimated at fewer than 2,000 birds worldwide.

sections.title: Why it's special
paras: Delhi-NCR has only a handful of past records: Okhla in 1992 and 2005, Palwal in 2004–05 and near Jewar in 2019. It shows that wetlands inside a megacity still matter to long-distance migrants.

stories.head: Beavers are back around Loch Ness: a family of six has been released about 500 years after they vanished
stories.dek: It's the first step in a plan to bring at least 15 beaver families back around the famous Scottish loch.
stat: since beavers lived around Loch Ness

sections.title: The release
paras: A family of six beavers was released on 4 November into a small lake on the 10,000-acre Dundreggan rewilding estate in Glenmoriston, in the Scottish Highlands. The Ness Beaver Project, run by Trees for Life and Beaver Trust, plans at least 15 beaver family groups around Loch Ness over three years. NatureScot licensed the release in October.

sections.title: Why beavers
paras: Beavers were hunted out of Britain centuries ago. Their dams slow rivers, which can cut downstream flooding, clean water and create wetlands that help many other species.

stories.credit: Solar car park / via Carbon Brief
stories.head: China's CO2 emissions fell 3.1% in July–September, the biggest quarterly drop since Covid
stories.dek: Clean power growth outpaced rising demand, and EVs hit a record 67% of new car sales in September.

sections.title: The analysis
paras: A Carbon Brief analysis published on 6 November found China's carbon emissions in July–September 2026 were 3.1% lower than a year earlier. Coal use fell 3% and oil use 4%. Electricity from solar, wind and nuclear grew by 110 TWh, more than twice the growth in total demand.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: China is the world's biggest emitter, so a lasting fall matters for the whole planet. Electric vehicles made up a record 67% of passenger car sales and 50% of heavy-truck sales in September. Analysts caution it's too early to call a peak, and high oil prices also played a part.

stories.head: 63 countries have now beaten at least one neglected tropical disease; sleeping sickness cases are down 98% since 1999
stories.dek: A WHO report shows 36% fewer people need treatment for these diseases than in 2010.
stat: countries that eliminated at least one NTD

sections.title: The progress
paras: According to a WHO report, about 1.41 billion people needed help against neglected tropical diseases in 2024, 36% fewer than in 2010. By June 2026, 63 countries had eliminated at least one of these diseases, up from 42 at the end of 2020. Togo became the first to eliminate four.

sections.title: Record lows
paras: Sleeping sickness cases have fallen 98% since 1999, and Guinea worm reached a record low of 10 human cases in 2025. WHO calls the progress uneven and fragile, with funding the biggest barrier.

stories.head: A baby who had about 110 seizures a day became seizure-free within 30 minutes of an experimental drug in Dubai
stories.dek: Genome sequencing found the exact faulty gene, letting doctors pick a targeted treatment.

sections.title: The case
paras: Baby Adnan was born with an extremely rare genetic epilepsy and had a seizure roughly every 13 minutes. Seven treatments failed. Whole-genome sequencing found the gene variant behind it, and doctors at King's College Hospital London – Dubai gave him the experimental oral drug ABS-1230 on a compassionate-use approval on 14 September. His seizures stopped within 30 minutes.

sections.title: Now
paras: He went home on 21 September and was still seizure-free at follow-ups into November. He is reported to be the youngest patient in the world to receive the drug. It's a single case, and doctors will keep monitoring him.

stories.credit: SS United States / via Billy Penn
stories.head: The SS United States, the fastest liner ever to cross the Atlantic, has been sunk off Florida to become the world's largest artificial reef
stories.dek: The 990-foot ship will now be a home for corals and fish, and a new site for divers.
stat: long, 108 ft longer than the Titanic

sections.title: The final voyage
paras: The historic liner was sunk on 11 November about 25 miles southwest of Destin, Florida, and now rests in about 180 feet of water, with its top deck about 60 feet below the surface. More than 863,000 people watched the livestream.

sections.title: A new life
paras: On its 1952 maiden voyage it set the transatlantic speed record, and it made more than 800 crossings before retiring in 1969. After months of cleaning out pollutants, the $13.5 million reef project gives sea life a huge new surface to settle on.
